content.text:
Mago combines four common PHP tool categories:

| Mago command | Roughly replaces |
|---|---|
| `mago analyze` | PHPStan, Psalm, Phan |
| `mago lint` | PHP_CodeSniffer (`phpcs`), parts of PHP-CS-Fixer, and `php -l` semantic checks |
| `mago format` / `fmt` | PHP-CS-Fixer formatting, Laravel Pint, `phpcbf`, Pretty PHP |
| `mago guard` | Deptrac, PHPArkitect |

Mago officially describes analyzer compatibility with PHPStan/Psalm annotations, and its guard as covering the same ground as Deptrac and Arkitect. [Mago tools](https://mago.carthage.software/main/en/tools/overview/), [Mago guard](https://mago.carthage.software/main/en/tools/guard/overview/)

It does not replace:

- PHPUnit or Mockery
- Composer
- Rector’s broad automated refactorings/migrations
- Runtime/integration tests
- `composer audit` or dedicated security scanners

For this repository, Mago currently supplements existing tools; it does not replace any listed `require-dev` dependency. PHPUnit, Mockery, vfsStream, and Amp Parallel serve different purposes.

content.text:
Use a layered workflow: formatter closest to editing, lint before commit, analyzer/guard before push, and CI as final enforcement.

| Tool | Purpose | Best daily timing | CI behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fmt` | Rewrites layout/style | Save or before commit | `fmt --check` |
| `lint` | Code smells, conventions, suspicious constructs | Before commit | `lint` |
| `analyze` | Types, invalid calls, logical errors | After meaningful edits or before push | `analyze` |
| `guard` | Architecture/dependency rules | After namespace/dependency changes | `guard` |

### Recommended for this repository

Daily:

```bash
make mago args='fmt --dry-run'
make mago args='lint'
make mago args='analyze'
```

Apply changes intentionally:

```bash
make mago args='fmt'
make mago args='lint --fix'
```

Before pushing:

```bash
make mago args='fmt --check'
make mago args='lint'
make mago args='analyze'
make mago args='guard'
```

`guard` currently adds little until `[guard]` rules are defined in `mago.toml`.

### IDE/autosave

Only formatting belongs on autosave. Linting and analysis should report diagnostics, not unexpectedly rewrite code.

Mago does not yet provide an LSP; its LSP is planned for 2.0. Therefore PhpStorm cannot currently use Mago like a native continuously-running inspection engine. You can configure a File Watcher/external formatter, but your current `make mago` starts a Docker Compose container, making it too heavyweight for every save. [Mago FAQ](https://mago.carthage.software/1.40.0/en/faq/)

Good options:

- Install the standalone Mago binary locally and configure PhpStorm’s File Watcher.
- Keep PhpStorm formatting-on-save disabled and run `make mago args='fmt'` manually.
- Add a keyboard shortcut for that Make target.

Mago supports formatting a single editor buffer through `format --stdin-input --stdin-filepath`, but that integration works best with a local binary. [Formatter integration](https://mago.carthage.software/main/en/tools/formatter/usage/)

### Git hooks

Hooks are optional convenience, not enforcement. Local `.git/hooks` are not committed, so CI remains necessary.

For this repository, I would use:

- Pre-commit: `fmt --check` and `lint`
- Pre-push: `analyze`, optionally `guard`
- CI: all enabled checks

One limitation: Mago’s useful `--staged` mode requires access to `.git`. Your current backend Compose container does not mount the repository’s `.git` directory, so this will likely not work:

```bash
make mago args='lint --staged'
```

Use whole-backend checks for now. Do not mount `.git` read-write merely to support a hook without considering the security and ownership implications. Mago officially supports staged linting/formatting when run directly in the working tree. [Pre-commit recipe](https://mago.carthage.software/1.41.0/en/recipes/pre-commit-hooks/)

### GitLab CI

Yes, CI should be authoritative. Add a backend quality job after `build-backend` and use the built development image. That image contains Composer dependencies, which the analyzer needs to resolve third-party types correctly. Mago’s standalone image works for formatting/linting, but its official documentation warns that analysis without Composer dependencies can produce undefined-symbol false positives. [Docker and GitLab CI recipe](https://mago.carthage.software/main/en/recipes/docker/)

Run:

```bash
mago fmt --check
mago lint
mago analyze
mago guard
```

Mago automatically selects GitLab-compatible reporting when `GITLAB_CI` is present. [Reporting formats](https://mago.carthage.software/main/en/fundamentals/shared-reporting-options/)

Before making CI blocking:

1. Run all checks locally.
2. Decide whether to make one dedicated formatting commit.
3. Configure or baseline existing lint/analyzer findings.
4. Define guard rules before enabling `guard`.

My practical recommendation: start with `lint` and `analyze` in CI, add `fmt --check` after a dedicated formatting commit, and add `guard` only after documenting actual architecture boundaries.

content.text:
Yes. Best fix: run Mago’s prebuilt image from Make using host UID/GID:

```make
MAGO_VERSION := 1.44.0

mago:
	docker run --rm\
			--user $(shell id -u):$(shell id -g)\
			--volume $(TC_BASE_DIR)/backend:/app\
			--workdir /app\
		ghcr.io/carthage-software/mago:$(MAGO_VERSION) $(args)
```

Benefits:

- Can rewrite host files
- No database/cache permission error
- No Mago download on every invocation
- No unnecessary DB/cache containers
- `vendor` remains available for analysis

Then:

```bash
make mago args='format src/controller/AssetAssignmentController.class.php'
```

Pin `MAGO_VERSION` to the Composer lock version to avoid behavior differences.
